content.thinking:
I'm going through the decision order: reject, escalate, return, incomplete, then approve, with the order procedure at 2.1. I'm looking at SOP 2.2, which says a claim can't be approved if any required fact is unknown, and I'm noting that the incomplete category is tied to that sentence rather than to the definition in section 1. Next I'm moving on to the rules in section 3, starting with 3.1 on claims submitted 61 days or more after the earliest date.

I'm working through the remaining rules in section 4 now: a line of $75 or more without an itemised receipt goes to return, any alcohol line goes to return, and gift lines for official recipients or business or first-class airfare go to escalate. I'm also noting that 4.5 carves out a pre-approved business-class exception that seems to conflict with 4.4, so I need to decide how to treat it.

I'm weighing whether the 4.5 pre-approval exception should stay as an approve rule, since escalate from 4.4 already takes precedence and it will never change the outcome. I'll translate it as written and let the conflict with 4.4 show up later, rather than reshaping the rule to fix it.

I'm now defining the cabin and category mappings, so business and first-class wording map to the same values, and alcohol and gift terms map to their categories.

I'm settling on how to map the categories and cabin terms, and deciding that the sections and subsections to cover are 1, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1 through 3.3, and 4.1 through 4.5.

I'm checking which section numbers the spec should cover, including the headings 2, 3 and 4 alongside their subsections. I'm also confirming that none of the rules need extra facts, since the receipt, pre-approval, official-recipient and total-amount facts already cover what the sections say.

I'm drafting the wording for the 4.4 airfare rule, the 3.3 director sign-off, and the 3.1 submission window, plus the unknown-facts sentence in 2.2.

I'm writing up the collection entry for the claim's lines, noting that the lines are unknown when the claim is empty and citing section 1 for the definition. Next I'm finishing the section 1 note on the outcomes and the Incomplete definition, and then writing out the JSON.

unknowns.text: A fact that has not been established is unknown, not false. If any fact required by this procedure is unknown, the claim cannot be approved.

lines.text: A claim is a list of lines, one per receipt or expense.

rules.text: Claims must be submitted within 60 days of the earliest expense on them. Reject a claim submitted 61 days or more after its earliest expense.
A claim's approver must not be the employee who submitted it. Reject a self-approved claim.
A claim totalling $5,000 or more needs the Finance Director's sign-off. Without it, escalate.
Every line of $75 or more needs an itemised receipt. If a receipt is missing or has not been attached, return the claim.
Alcohol is not reimbursable. Return any claim with a line for alcohol.
A gift to a government official must be reviewed under the anti-bribery policy. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class and first-class airfare must be reviewed. Escalate any claim with such a line.
Business-class airfare pre-approved in writing by the Finance Director may be approved.

sections.note: Purpose: defines the five outcomes and that a claim is a list of lines; used for the outcome names and the 'lines' collection's unknown_when_empty. Sets no rule of its own.
Heading only; its content is in 2.1 and 2.2.
Sets what a possibly-applying rule with an unknown fact leads to (unknowns -> incomplete).
Heading only; its content is in 3.1 to 3.3.
Heading only; its content is in 4.1 to 4.5.

Translated as written. It is an exception to 4.4, but under 2.1 the Escalate outcome from 4.4 always outranks Approve. Every case where this rule applies also meets 4.4, so this rule can never decide the outcome. A person should decide how 4.4 and 4.5 are meant to interact.
